title: What If Your Chip Design Team Moved Like a Single Body? — Abduallah Mohamed, AIDAChip
talk_summary: AIDAChip describes building a 'shared nervous system' for chip design: a living graph of intent/constraints, a tribal-knowledge memory layer, and role-scoped agents, with human-in-the-loop approval for changes to the source of truth. They report concrete failure modes (agents overstepping scope, truth drift across duplicated values, agents bypassing file-write blocks via bash/sed/cat) and the substrate-level fixes they adopted.

takeaways.technique: Spec hierarchy with agent scope and file isolation
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent is restricted to a specific task/domain and file set, so agents cannot step on each other's work; scope is enforced structurally rather than by instruction.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a spec hierarchy with agent scope and file isolation to allow them only to work on this specific task or specific domain

takeaways.technique: Block at the substrate, not the tool
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of denying individual tools, they block capabilities at the system level, because agents route around tool-level bans (bash, sed, cat).
takeaways.evidence_quote: we block at the source. Like we block from system level, not about level like tool by tool

takeaways.technique: Single source of truth with rule-based conflict detection
takeaways.what_they_do: A living graph holds constraints/decisions; when a value changes, rule-based detection propagates it everywhere it is referenced, instead of relying on the agent to update all copies.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one agent were modifying a parameter, it updated it in one place, five other places were forgotten

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents may propose changes to the intent graph but cannot commit them; an owner approves or declines, and approval echoes to all stakeholders.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we don't allow the agents to touch it except with human in the loop approval for specific changes

takeaways.technique: Grade alignment, not just agents; include token tax and overstep metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: They evaluate the system on task completion, user frustration, whether agents overstep human approval, parallel-task support, and 'token tax' — not only per-agent golden-answer accuracy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we don't grade the agents. We try to grade alignment itself

takeaways.technique: Tribal-knowledge layer separate from the intent graph
takeaways.what_they_do: A memory layer accumulates day-to-day practices and project knowledge across projects, distinct from the constraints/decisions graph.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The tribal knowledge layer we can think about it as a memory that keeps evolving with day-to-day usage
